title: What Happens If You Crack Your Knuckles Every Day?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Is Cracking Your Knuckles Bad for You?' (the pop involves gas in the synovial fluid that lubricates your finger joints; long-held view: the gas bubbles and bursts; a 2015 study suggests a gas-filled cavity forming; Dr. Baker compares it to uncorking a wine bottle; popping your knuckles won't cause arthritis, several studies failed to show an association; as long as you're not feeling pain or having swelling it's probably OK; cracking shouldn't cause pain; if you notice swelling see a healthcare provider): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/is-cracking-your-knuckles-bad-for-you

Harvard Health Publishing, 'Knuckle cracking: Annoying and harmful, or just annoying?' (increasing the space between finger joints causes gas bubbles in the joint fluid to collapse or burst; you can't crack the same knuckle again right away because it takes time for the gas bubbles to accumulate again; a California doctor cracked the knuckles of only one hand and after decades x-rays showed no difference in arthritis between his hands; a 1990 study of 74 crackers and 226 non-crackers found the same incidence of arthritis, and a larger study reached a similar conclusion): https://www.health.harvard.edu/blog/knuckle-cracking-annoying-and-harmful-or-just-annoying-2018051413797

Scientific American, 'Crack Research: Good news about knuckle cracking' (Dr. Donald Unger cracked the knuckles of his left hand at least twice a day for about 50 years, leaving the right hand as a control; 'no arthritis in either hand, and no apparent differences between the two hands'; Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine 2009; original letter: Unger DL, Arthritis Rheum 1998;41(5):949-50): https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/crack-research/

lines.text: What happens if you crack your knuckles every day?
but first, what's actually making that pop?
Your knuckles sit in slippery joint fluid,
Pull the joint apart, the space widens,
and the gas goes pop, like uncorking a bottle.
That gas needs time to build back up,
so you can't crack it again right away.
So, arthritis? One doctor tested it on himself.
For fifty years, he cracked his left hand
at least twice a day, and never his right.
Result? No arthritis in either hand, and bigger studies agree.
If it hurts or swells, see a doctor.
